name: Fragrance clones (dupes) / Zara

lead: Clones, or dupes, are budget perfumes made to smell like famous designer or niche fragrances, so you can wear a similar scent for much less. Zara, the fast-fashion chain, sells perfumes and is a frequent topic in fragrance communities.

Producers analyse best-selling perfumes, often with gas chromatography, and formulate similar-smelling blends. Community members value the price gap; independent comparative research on how close dupes are to the originals was not found.

paras: Buyers read community comparisons to find which budget scent matches a designer one they like, then try it in store or from a sample. Many wear a dupe for daily use and keep an original for special occasions.

Copyright protection for scents is unsettled, and courts in different countries have ruled differently. As with any perfume, fragrance ingredients can cause skin allergies or asthma reactions in some people.

angle.text: Lookalike perfumes let you wear a scent close to an expensive designer release at a low price. The pleasant smell is noticeable as soon as you put it on. Online fragrance communities discuss Zara and similar brands as common sources.

lead: Fragrance clones, or 'dupes', are inexpensive perfumes made to smell like well-known designer or niche fragrances. People use them to smell good on a small budget: scent is part of how someone is perceived, and clones let a person wear a signature designer-style fragrance for a fraction of the price. Zara, the Spanish fast-fashion retailer owned by Inditex, sells perfumes and launched a beauty line in 2021, and its fragrances are a frequent subject in dupe discussions [1].

A looksmax.org thread introducing fragrance clones describes them as copies of a certain scent at much lower prices, with a poster claiming a designer fragrance costing hundreds of dollars can be matched for around $30 and comparing clones to 'reps' of clothing and sneakers [2]. In a reply, another user says he never focused on scent until he met a guy who always smells good and that the thread made him want to buy a fragrance [2].

Reverse engineering of best-selling perfumes is described as common in the industry, since gas chromatography equipment is relatively simple to operate and the market is lucrative [3]. Whether a fragrance can be protected by copyright is unsettled, and courts in different countries have ruled differently [3].

paras: Perfume formulas can be analysed with gas chromatography–mass spectrometry, which reveals a general formula, although natural oils complicate the analysis [3]. A related practice, 'numbered perfumery' in ex-USSR countries, sells generic-bottled products labelled as an aroma 'in the direction of' a known perfume [3].

Zara is described as a fast-fashion company that brings products to stores far faster than the industry average, and it sells clothing, accessories, beauty products and perfumes [1]. Its encyclopedic entry does not discuss fragrance dupes specifically, though it records fashion-design copying disputes in 2016 and 2018 [1].

A 2021 StyleCaster article republished by Yahoo reported that a Zara perfume called Red Temptation, 80 mL at $25.90, was going viral on TikTok with users calling it a dupe of Maison Francis Kurkdjian's Baccarat Rouge 540, listed at $325 [4]. One TikTok user is quoted saying it smells 'pretty much the same' but that she could tell the difference [4]. The article also reports a TikTok user calling Zara Gardenia a dupe for YSL Black Opium and Zara Applejuice a dupe for Chanel Chance Eau Tendre [4]. These are informal user impressions rather than side-by-side tests.

Fragrance is discussed in appearance and grooming communities as a low-cost way to improve presentation. In the looksmax.org clones thread, the original poster presents clones as a summer, party and date-night option and says clone sellers use different names and producers for each scent, which he says makes them harder to sort through than designer originals [2].

It is doubtful that perfumes qualify for US copyright and no US court has ruled on the matter; a scent cannot be trademarked because it is functional [3]. The Dutch Supreme Court granted copyright protection to Lancôme's Trésor in 2006, while the French Supreme Court has twice held that perfumes lack the necessary creativity [3]. Knock-offs sometimes use slightly altered names [3].

Perfume ingredients are regulated differently by region; the EU requires 26 recognised fragrance allergens to be listed above set thresholds [3]. Fragrance can trigger skin allergy, headaches and asthma reactions in some people [3]. No study found compared clone and original fragrances on safety or longevity.

lore.intro: On looksmax.org, clones are introduced as an inexpensive way to smell good, compared with 'reps' in clothing and sneakers.

claims.claim: A clone can match an expensive designer fragrance for a fraction of the price
Smelling good is a meaningful part of presentation

timeline.event: EU rules begin requiring 26 fragrance allergens to be listed.[3]
Dutch Supreme Court grants copyright protection to Lancôme's Trésor.[3]
Zara launches its first beauty line.[1]
